metadata.course_description: Laboratory component of Electrical Circuits 2 covering AC power measurement, power factor improvement, series/parallel resonance, three-phase wye and delta circuits, and two-wattmeter power measurements.
metadata.workload_description:
With 18 weeks at 3 contact hours per week (54 contact hours total) the expected student workload is as follows:
• Group Activities for Formative Assessment
• Total of 4 quizzes (2 for both Midterm and Final Term)
• Midterm and Final Examinations
In instances where face-to-face sessions are impractical, online sessions, asynchronous class, or their equivalent will be provided.
metadata.passing_grade_conditions: Students shall take all assessments and examinations and must have an attendance of not less than 80% in the class. In case of lacking output or examination, a grade of INC (Incomplete) shall be given in accordance with the existing rules and regulations reflected in the student handbook. In case of incurring absences of more than 20% of the total expected number of attendances, a grade of UW (Unauthorized Withdrawal) will be reflected in the grade sheet.

sdg_table.description: This course introduces the core concepts of electrical power, energy-storing elements (capacitors and inductors), and maximum power transfer. A rigorous understanding of voltage, current, and power calculation is the absolute prerequisite for designing, analyzing, and optimizing renewable energy systems, smart grids, and energy-efficient electrical networks in the future.

Circuit analysis is the fundamental language of all electrical infrastructure and technological innovation. By learning to simplify complex multi-source networks and analyze transient and steady-state responses, students develop the technical competencies required to innovate and maintain resilient industrial power systems, electronics, and communication infrastructures.

syllabus_assessment_activities.description: Collaborative, team-based projects or assessments where students analyze, calculate, and simulate fundamental DC and AC electrical networks (e.g., verifying Thevenin/Norton equivalent circuits, or evaluating RLC transient responses). This integrates theoretical mathematical modeling with circuit simulation software to reinforce core circuit analysis principles and develop foundational engineering problem-solving skills.

Periodic summative assessments comprising conceptual questions and structured mathematical problem-solving scenarios. Designed to incrementally evaluate the students' analytical grasp of fundamental circuit laws, network theorems, energy-storing elements, and AC/DC circuit analysis techniques prior to major examinations.

Comprehensive summative assessments designed to evaluate the students' overall mastery of the course material. These proctored examinations require students to synthesize knowledge through a rigorous mix of conceptual theoretical questions, complex electrical network analysis, and multi-step mathematical problem-solving scenarios (e.g., nodal and mesh analysis, application of equivalent circuit theorems, RLC transient responses, and frequency-domain phasor analysis).

policies_table.title: Attendance and Punctuality
policies_table.description: Classroom attendance is an integral part of the educational experience; therefore, it is the student's responsibility to attend class. Attendance will be checked at every meeting. A student who accumulates exceeding 20% of the prescribed number of class hours will automatically be dropped from the course (unexcused absences). Arriving 15 minutes after the scheduled start time constitutes a late mark. Three late marks equate to one unexcused absence.

policies_table.title: Behavior and Decorum
policies_table.description: Respectful, inclusive, and professional behavior is always expected. The use of polite and non-discriminatory language is strictly observed in line with the University's commitment to a gender-fair and inclusive learning environment, and adherence to RA 11313, also known as the Safe Spaces Act.

policies_table.title: Gadget Use
policies_table.description: Mobile phones, tablets, and laptops must be stowed away during standard lectures to minimize distractions. However, laptops are expressively permitted and encouraged during designated practical sessions, such as when developing scripts for laboratory data automation or running circuit simulations.

policies_table.title: Dress Code
policies_table.description: Wearing the prescribed university uniform is a must in accordance with the Student Handbook.

policies_table.title: Submission of Coursework
policies_table.description:
Extensions and late submissions of requirements will only be considered if done in writing to the lecturer at least two days before the due date. Generally, no extension will be given for the assignments.
• Should work be submitted after the due date without written approval for an extension, a penalty of 5% deduction from the grade will be incurred for every 2 days it is late.
• Should the work be assessed as being close to a PASS grade, but the standard has not yet been fully met, the lecturer may offer the opportunity to resubmit.

policies_table.title: Use of AI Tools
policies_table.description: The responsible use of generative AI tools (e.g., ChatGPT, Grammarly, Quillbot) is permitted only when explicitly allowed by the instructor for specific tasks. All AI-assisted work must be properly cited or declared.

policies_table.title: Academic Honesty
policies_table.description:
All USePians are bound to follow the rules and regulations stipulated in the student handbook of the University and the College. Academic dishonesty includes cheating in any form, plagiarism, and similar offenses.
• Cheating on any assignment or examination incurs a minimum penalty of zero for that work and referral to OSAS.
• Submitting AI-generated content as original work without disclosure is considered academic dishonesty (max 15% similarity threshold).

policies_table.title: Conduct of Quizzes and Examinations
policies_table.description:
• Keep calculator jackets, smartphones, and irrelevant items inside bags.
• Do not round off intermediate values to avoid accumulated rounding errors; final answers must be in three decimal places.
• Write legibly using black or blue ballpoint pen and show all pertinent solutions clearly.
• Math plate is used during quizzes and bluebook for term examinations.
• No special quizzes or examinations will be given except for valid, documented reasons.

policies_table.title: Use of Calculators
policies_table.description: Allowed calculators must follow the Professional Regulatory Commission (PRC) recommendations (https://www.prc.gov.ph/node/6984) for non-programmable calculators.

policies_table.title: Group Work and Independent Effort
policies_table.description: Every group must ensure equitable contributions from all members. Directly sharing completed circuits, code, or written reports across groups is considered plagiarism and will result in a zero (0) for all involved parties.

policies_table.title: Cleanliness and Energy Conservation
policies_table.description: Observe cleanliness before and after class. Ensure all plugged devices and lights are turned off before leaving the classroom.

policies_table.title: Communication Channels
policies_table.description: Official announcements and course updates will be posted via the USeP Virtual Environment (UVE), email, or official class group chat. Direct communication with the instructor must be conducted strictly during official working days and hours (Monday to Friday, 8:00 AM to 5:00 PM).

indicators.remarks: Conducive learning environment maintained in accordance with University policies.

cqi_plan.key_strengths: Course delivery strictly followed the OBE syllabus learning plan, utilizing problem-based learning, collaborative group activities (FA1), and structured rubric-based summative assessments (SA1 & SA2).
cqi_plan.areas_for_improvement: Some students encountered difficulties in setting up multi-loop nodal/mesh differential equations and time-domain RLC transient analysis under time constraints during major examinations.
cqi_plan.action_plan:
1. Increase guided problem-solving drills and simulation verification during formative group activities (FA1).
2. Conduct targeted remedial review sessions prior to term examinations focusing on CLOs with <75% average score.
3. Provide step-by-step rubric exemplars for multi-source network theorem and transient problems.
